ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the Spanish Official State Gazette (BOE), the European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, and Bank of Spain measures. Enhanced due diligence is required under Articles 4, 10 and 14 of Ley 10/2010, including verification of identity, source of funds, source of wealth, beneficial ownership, commercial purpose, and continuous monitoring of PEPs and persons from high-risk third countries.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) — https://www.rmc.es (name clearance section, 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names must be written in Spanish or any co-official Spanish language using Latin alphabet characters with Spanish orthography. Foreign terms are permissible only if transliterated into Roman/Latin script and grammatically compatible; the name may not include expressions contrary to law, public order or fundamental rights, and must not be identical or phonetically/graphically confusingly similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate remains valid for 90 calendar days from issuance; no automatic extension exists, and a fresh application may be filed before expiry to re-secure the same name if it has not been occupied. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' with the Central Mercantile Registry within one month of notification, and subsequently a 'recurso contencioso-administrativo' before the Administrative Chamber of the Spanish National Court within two months. Alternatively, a new application with a modified name may be submitted without exhausting administrative remedies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or serviced address is permitted for an SL only if it provides a physical premises in Spain where legal notifications can be received, statutory books are maintained, and supervisory authorities can inspect activities. For the ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical trading scope (AML Medium-Risk Enhanced), a pure virtual mailbox is inadvisable; a dedicated serviced office with management presence and documentation storage is the minimum acceptable commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 20% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a standard SL with a dedicated physical office; approximately 45% if a virtual-only or subaddressing arrangement is used.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act), Articles 4, 19-27 and 62-66; Law 18/2022 'Crea y Crece' (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Ley 14/2013 and Real Decreto 1270/2003 (notarial and registry fee schedules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, for the negative name certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) signed before a Notary and inscribed in the Mercantile Registry, together with the AEAT tax form Modelo 600 for stamp duty (AJ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The share capital must be fully subscribed and paid in at constitution. Standard SL minimum paid-up capital is EUR 3,000; under the Law 18/2022 Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime the minimum may be reduced to EUR 1, with restrictions on dividend distribution and profit application until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached. Capital is evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso); no statutory escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscribed share capital, fully paid in and evidenced by the bank deposit certificate, is duly accepted, and each founding member's shareholding is approved as recorded in the deed. (2) That the registered office of the company is adopted at [address], within the municipality of [city], Spain. (3) That the following persons are appointed to the joint office of administrator(s): [Name(s)], accepting the office and acknowledging the powers conferred. (4) That the administration is authorized to open national bank accounts and to transact LC financing operations, to execute all supplementary notarial and registry deeds, and to apply for the company's CIF/NIF and municipal operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Negative Name Certificate (Certificado de Denominación Social Negativa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid — online portal www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name certificate application electronically through the Registro Mercantil Central platform, proposing up to three alternative company names ending in 'Sociedad Limitada' or 'SL'. Pay the official tasa fee (approximately EUR 20). The certificate confirming that no identical or confusingly similar name is registered is issued valid for three months and must be delivered to the notary at execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Completed name application form (modelo de solicitud)
NIE or valid passport of the founding partners
Where a corporate founder exists, its certificate of incorporation and legal representation attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected for identity or similitude, immediately resubmit the application with alternative denominations; no formal administrative appeal is available for the name certificate itself.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining NIE for Non-Resident Founders and Administrators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oficina de Extranjería de la Delegación del Gobierno or assigned Comisaría de Policía Nacional in the applicant's province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete form EX-15, attach a valid passport and, where applicable, the entry visa or residence permit, indicating the SL incorporation as justification for the NIE application. Pay tasa 790-012 and attend the biometric appointment at the police station, where the NIE certificate is issued; the certificate must be presented to the notary and to the bank.
required_dossiers: Form EX-15 (solicitud de NIE)
Valid passport or national identity document
Proof of address in the place of application
Payment receipt of tasa 790-012
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a police requerimiento for additional evidence, provide notarized proof of funds for the share subscription and a sponsorship declaration; reschedule a new appointment within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Provisional Bank Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (entidad de crédito) with a branch acceptant of non-resident corporate founders (e.g., BBVA, Santander, CaixaBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the negative name certificate, the NIE of all founders, and the draft incorporation documents. Open the provisional account in the name of the 'Sociedad Limitada en constitución', transfer the full share capital, and instruct the bank to issue the certificado de desembolso (capital deposit certificate) addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Certificado negativo de denominación
NIE of each founding member
Passport and power of attorney of the account signatory
Source-of-wealth statement for the AML/KYB enhanced due-diligence review triggered by the petrochemical trading scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank prolongs AML review, file parallel applications with two candidate banks and submit the full KYC packet simultaneously; an internal compliance escalation is available under the bank's remediation protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) of the province where the registered office is established, registered with the competent Colegio Notarial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding partners must appear in person or through a duly notarized power of attorney before the chosen notary. The notary verifies legal capacity, any criminal record certificates of designated administrators, and the deposit certificate; the deed containing the articles of association (estatutos) and the first appointment of administrators is executed. The notary thereafter transmits the deed telematized to the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Certificado de denominación social (valid not more than three months)
Certificado de depósito bancario of the share capital
NIE of all founders or their notarial proxy holder
Certificado de antecedentes penales for each appointed administrator (EU citizens) or equivalent declaration
Draft articles of association (estatutos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to grant the deed owing to defective documentation, correct the title defects by supplementary affidavit and schedule a new execution appointment; legal-capacity issues are cured by appointing a valid proxy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional and Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF/CIF) and Censal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Oficina de Gestión Tributaria via Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month from execution of the deed, submit the form Modelo 030 (declaración censal) attaching the notarial copy. The AEAT issues the provisional NIF; upon inscription in the Mercantile Registry, the same authority converts it to the definitive CIF of the SL. The CIF is required for all later registrations.
required_dossiers: Copia autorizada / testimonio telemático of the incorporation deed
Certificado de denominación negativa
NIE of the legal representative filing the declaration
Modelo 030 duly completed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT rejects the filing for lack of representation, file a corrective position with a notarized power of attorney translated into Spanish; if the one-month deadline is missed, the late filing surcharge regime applies and must be regularized immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Mercantile Registry and Payment of Stamp Duty (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office province, via the notary's telematic channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the copia autorizada of the deed to the Provincial Registry within ten days of signature. The registrar examines the legality of the deed and inscribes the company. Simultaneously, the representative pays stamp duty via Modelo 600 within 30 days of the deed, at the rate of 1% of the paid-in capital (unless an autonomous community exemption applies).
required_dossiers: Notarial testimony (copia autorizada) transmitted by the notary
Modelo 600 self-assessment form evidencing payment
Registry fee arancel certificate
Statement of no statutory disqualifications for administrators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'nota de defectos' (qualification of defects), the company must cure the defects within the stated calendar period, usually 15 to 30 days, by executing a supplementary deed or notarial amendment before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with Social Security and Occupational Risk Prevention Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) — ImportaSS / System RED; external prevention service (Servicio de Prevención Ajeno, SPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File form TA.7 (inscripción de empresario) electronically to obtain the corporate employer number (CCC). Appoint the employer representative and execute a contract with a registered SPA for occupational risk prevention under Ley 31/1995 before any hiring; this includes the workplace assessment and the initial prevention plan.
required_dossiers: Provisional or definitive CIF of the SL
Copy of the registration certificate in the Mercantile Registry
Certificate of deed inscription
Contract with the Servicio de Prevención Ajeno including warehousing risks
Company workbook (primer establecimiento) if the first employee is enrolled
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: TGSS rejections for NIF mismatches are cured by rectifying the Modelo 030 censal declaration and resubmitting TA.7 with the corrected identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating and Opening License (Licencia de Actividad y Apertura) with Environmental and Waste Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento (municipal council) of the warehouse location; autonomous community environmental authority (Dirección General de Calidad Ambiental) where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the declaración responsable or the application for the municipal activity and opening license through the municipal electronic platform, attaching the licensed technical project (proyecto técnico), fire safety certificate, and urban-planning compatibility certificate. For waste-producing establishments, register in the regional waste producer register under Ley 7/2022 and obtain the environmental classification for the wholesale distribution activity.
required_dossiers: Technical project signed by a licensed architect or engineer
Fire safety certificate issued in accordance with Real Decreto 2267/2004
Certificado urbanístico (land-use compatibility)
Waste registration forms under Ley 7/2022 (modelo de comunicación de productor de residuos)
Environmental self-assessment classification demonstrating exemption from full EIA under Ley 21/2013
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal requerimientos for building or fire-code non-compliance are cured by submitting a supplementary technical response addressing each defect; if the license is refused, an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) lies before the autonomous community commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo (General Directorate of Industry) for industrial establishment registration; autonomous community industry service (Consejería de Industria / Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas); and the municipal Ayuntamiento for the activity and opening license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de actividad y apertura de establecimiento (municipal operating and opening license for a commercial wholesale warehouse); alternatively, Declaración Responsable de inicio de actividad for premises classified as innocuous or without significant environmental impact.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) — Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental; implementation delegated to the autonomous community environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full 'Proyecto de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental' under Ley 21/2013: wholesale distribution and storage of virgin polyolefin granules is not listed in Annexes I or II, provided the storage thresholds for hazardous substances under the Seveso III regime (Real Decreto 840/2015 / Real Decreto 118/2020) are not crossed. The activity is subject to simplified municipal environmental classification (actividad clasificada) and, where applicable, regional environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with municipal sewer by-laws and Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2001 (Ley de Aguas), with pre-treatment of any floor run-off; discharge limits generally suspended solids < 500 mg/L, COD < 750 mg/L, hydrocarbons < 15 mg/L. Atmospheric: Real Decreto 102/2011 limit values, PM10 daily mean 50 µg/m³ (24 hours) and annual 40 µg/m³, with fugitive pellet-dust containment measures at transfer points. Waste: Ley 7/2022 de residuos y suelos contaminados, non-hazardous plastic waste codes LER 07 02 13 / 19 12 04, segregated labelled storage and traceable record under Real Decreto 553/1990.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the industrial warehouse under Real Decreto 2267/2004 (Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios en Establecimientos Industriales) and the CTE DB-SI building code; structural load validation of floors and racking systems under CTE DB-SE; workplace health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997 covering evacuation routes, lighting, climate, sanitation, first-aid facilities, and emergency plans; all permissions must be recorded in the company's official workplace inspection documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal at www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish resident entities obtain NIF at incorporation via the Mercantile Registry. Non-resident entities procure NIF through AEAT by submitting form 036 or online registration for tax purposes, followed by tax identification number issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available. Spain applies entity-level taxation with territorial scope for certain income categories and hybrid mismatch adjustments under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory implementation of Facturae electronic invoicing system requiring digital stamps (sello electrónico) for all VAT-liable invoices. Large taxpayers must comply with real-time reporting and API integration with AEAT systems for clearance and stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and services to non-EU customers. Eligibility requires proof that the goods are exported outside the EU or services rendered to non-residents, with supporting documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of zero-rating on exports result in penalties of up to 100% of the evaded VAT plus interest. Retrospective clawback applies if export documentation is insufficient or false, with potential criminal prosecution for intentional fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the central monetary authority and competent statistical authority for external transactions, jointly with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business), which operates the Foreign Investment Registry and the capital-movement control framework under Law 19/2003 of 4 July 2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, and Spain applies no exchange-control restrictions on either current-account flows (trade settlement, service fees, dividends, interest, royalties) or capital-account operations (equity injections, intra-group loans, securities, acquisitions) with EU/EEA counterparties under Article 63 TFEU. For third countries, Law 19/2003 maintains unrestricted movement of capital subject only to: (i) statistical declaration obligations to Banco de España under Circular 4/2023; (ii) EU/CFSP restrictive measures and sanctions screening; (iii) anti-money-laundering verification under Law 10/2010; and (iv) foreign-investment screening under Regulation (EU) 2019/452 for investments affecting security, critical infrastructure, or sensitive technology. Non-resident profit remittance by an SL shareholder is free of FX approval; the only practical hurdles are corporate tax certification (dividend withholding at 19% where applicable, plus Form 210/211 filing) and the bank's internal compliance sign-off. Multi-currency accounts (EUR, USD, CNY, MXN, BRL) may be opened freely, and trade invoices may be denominated in any currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Spain. The SL may retain 100% of export proceeds in EUR or in foreign currency and may dispose of them freely. The only obligations are statistical: banks aggregate and file BE-1 transaction declarations on behalf of clients, while clients must directly file BE-2 declarations to Banco de España for individual cross-border transactions exceeding the quantitative thresholds set in Circular 4/2023, and BE-3 position declarations for foreign-currency and external assets/liabilities balances. No 30-day conversion window, no repatriation quota, and no Central Bank approval is required for polymer export settlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Current Account (EUR/USD) with documentary credit and trade-finance collateral line
Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito de Capital Social / Certificate of Deposit for notarized subscription) convertible to Operational EUR Account
Operational EUR Current Account with ancillary cash-pooling and supply-chain services
Operational EUR/USD Account with working-capital and guarantees line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an ancillary payment rail and LOW as the primary cross-border treasury rail for this ISIC 4669 wholesale business. Spanish e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions regulated under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 (transposed by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018) may lawfully open and operate payment accounts, process SWIFT/SEPA transfers, and provide FX conversion; however, they cannot extend credit, open or negotiate commercial letters of credit, issue guarantees, or act as correspondent banks for documentary collections. An SL executing bulk petrochemical polymer trade must therefore maintain its irrevocable LC and settlement infrastructure at a licensed credit institution. Offshore EMIs (e.g., post-Brexit UK payment firms) have lost EU passporting and require a Spanish branch authorization from Banco de España; reliance on such providers alone would be incompatible with the target payment rails and would trigger bank de-risking responses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or notarial verification is effectively mandatory. Spanish banks applying Law 10/2010 enhanced due diligence to a Medium-Risk_Enhanced wholesale entity with non-resident ultimate owners will require: (i) a scheduled in-person interview at the branch for the appointed legal representative (administrador) or, alternatively, for a Spanish-resident attorney-in-fact holding a general power of attorney granted before a notary, apostilled and sworn-translated; (ii) verification of the beneficial owner's identity with a valid passport; (iii) a corporate-variation protocol evidencing the shareholder resolution approving the banking relationship; and (iv) confirmation of the physical office address in Spain. Remote video-identification is accepted only for domestic low-risk retail clients and is not a realistic route for this profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows to or from high-risk or embargoed jurisdictions (e.g., certain Latin American, Middle Eastern, or African polymer suppliers) generating sanctions or PEP-list hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and UN Security Council screening certificates; complete counterparty KYC packs; Incoterms 2020 purchase/sale contracts; UCP 600-compliant letters of credit and bills of lading/CMR waybills; EUR1/end-use certificates confirming non-dual-use bulk plastics; customs entry summary declarations (EORI-linked).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain or a non-resident ultimate shareholder unable to demonstrate the source of funds used for the capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and sworn-translated certificate of incorporation and registry abstracts of each intermediate shareholder; statutory beneficial-owner declarations filed under Law 10/2010; the SL's Libro Registro de Socios; source-of-funds evidence (12-month bank statements, audited parent-company financial statements, share-acquisition deed proving origin of capital).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangular trade pattern: invoices and settlements moving through third countries inconsistent with the stated physical supply chain, or abrupt high-turnover spikes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 18-month treasury and liquidity projection; full trade-cycle narrative (order, LC issuance, shipment, inspection, settlement); open-contract register; port receipts and warehouse storage documents; VAT/customs extracts (Modelo 303, Single Administrative Document) showing physical goods movement; audited annual accounts for the SL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of economic substance in Spain: foreign-resident management, no local premises, and no payroll or social-security footprint in the jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish substance file: execution of office lease, registration with Seguridad Social, local director passes NIE and tax registration, corporate meeting minutes signed in Spain, designated tax representative for Hacienda, and the SL's valid CIF plus evidence of active VAT/payroll returns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the initial paid-in capital of the SL: SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's account to the SL's EUR IBAN (TARGET2/SEPA interoperable). Field 50a must identify the remitting shareholder; field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Aporte de capital social — suscripción de participaciones' followed by the public-deed number and date; field 72 should reference the notarial authorization. If the funds are deposited before incorporation, they must be placed in a blocked escrow deposit account certified by the bank (Certificado de Depósito) addressed to the notary. The verification package comprises: notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución), share-subscription list (lista de suscripción), capital-payment certificate, and notary's declaration of compliance with Law 14/2013. Concurrently, the SL must file the declaración de inversión exterior with the Foreign Investment Registry under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023 within the statutory filing window, using the official DIA (Declaración Informativa de Inversión Exterior) form including the purpose code 1110 (investment by non-residents in shares of a Spanish limited company). The receiving bank mirrors the transaction in its BE-2/4 statistical declarations. Shareholder loans must be documented as a separate 'participación financiera' transaction with a distinct concept to prevent re-characterization as hidden equity contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for bulk polyethylene and polypropylene purchases: (i) Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600, communicated via SWIFT MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), MT754 (advice) and settled through MT103/MT202 cover payments with MT400/MT412 reimbursement where applicable; (ii) Standby Letter of Credit (MT760) for supplier security margins; (iii) SWIFT MT103 for open-account and advance-payment disbursements to verified suppliers, using the correspondent clearing network of the issuing Spanish bank with the USD nostro chain; and (iv) SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT/XML ISO 20022) for low-value intra-EU settlements. For LatAm-bound flows, clearing through Banco Santander or BBVA correspondent networks reduces friction and permits same-day value. All outbound disbursements must carry the correct purpose classification for the Banco de España statistical declaration (purpose code 4200 for trade credits, 4300 for goods trade settlement), reference the commercial invoice and Incoterms delivery stage, and must be screened against the EU/OFAC/UN sanctions lists before initiation. Commercial LCs should be denominated in USD for Middle Eastern and Asian master-batch suppliers and in EUR for intra-EU counterparties, with swap-in-place hedging to match the SL's EUR base.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX Forwards (physical delivery), typically 1-week to 12-month tenors, executed under an ISDA 2002 master agreement or the Spanish Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF), with EMIR transaction reporting to a registered trade repository and no central-clearing obligation for vanilla foreign-exchange forwards.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restrictive LatAm and emerging-market currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Venezuelan bolívar, Nigerian naira) referenced to EUR/USD, permitted for bona fide trade-hedging purposes, subject to EMIR reporting, Banco de España statistical declaration, and documented underlying exposure.

Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD fixed-for-fixed) aligned with the maturity profile of the import trade-finance book, negotiated under the bank's Credit Support Annex to cover principal and interest re-pricing risk on USD-denominated polymer inventory purchases.

FX Swaps (swap de divisas) for periodic conversion and reconversion of USD export receipts into EUR operating cash, permissible only where a continuous underlying trade-exposure schedule and the SL's treasury policy substantiate the transaction; transactions are reported to Banco de España under the BE statistical framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) including auditor's report where mandatory and beneficial-owner identification sheet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office; central publication in the Official Gazette of the Mercantile Registry (BORME)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers a fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 12,000, closure of the company's registry file, and blockage of registration of corporate acts; persistent non-filing can result in dissolution and eventual strike-off after liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days after the six-month period following the tax year-end; for calendar-year filers, between 1 and 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues a 5%–20% surcharge plus late-payment interest; underestimations or omissions attract assessment penalties of 50%–100%, with possible seizure of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 30 January following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing carries penalties up to 15% of the tax amount, flat procedural fines, and late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership data embedded in the deposited annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil as part of the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the annual accounts deposit: within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or false UBO information triggers anti-money-laundering fines under Law 10/2010, registry closure, and rejection of annual accounts deposit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required if the SL meets at least two of the following three conditions for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Audit is also required when the entity is part of a group filing consolidated accounts or when ordered by a court or the Mercantile Registry.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) as approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007; listed groups apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU; wholesale distribution companies use the standard PGC framework unless a sector-specific adaptation applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must provide beneficial-owner identification as part of the annual accounts deposit. Upon any shareholding transfer, the administrators must update the Register of Members within 15 days and record the resulting change of ultimate beneficial ownership in the internal UBO records within one month. Spain does not impose a standalone annual UBO return; instead, annual confirmation is made through the annual accounts deposit at the Mercantile Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Journal and Inventories / Balance Sheet Book
Register of Sole-Shareholder Contracts (if sole shareholder)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spanish resident SL companies are generally taxed at 25%. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Qualifying newly created companies and qualifying start-ups may receive additional relief under the Start-ups Law. Companies with prior-year net turnover below EUR 1 million may qualify for the applicable reduced SME rate and transitional rate rules. Tax depreciation, impairment restrictions, R&D deductions, capitalization deductions, reserve deductions, participation exemption rules, and treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may reduce the effective rate. Spanish tax losses generally carry forward indefinitely, subject to utilization limits and anti-abuse rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments; filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is filed within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to AEAT calendar adjustments and payment arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period dates, entity type, turnover classification, group status, and accounting regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL is a resident corporate taxpayer. A non-resident shareholder, lender, or supplier is reported through its foreign identification and tax-residence information where required; it does not replace the SL's Spanish NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Balance sheet and profit and loss account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, expenses, financial result, extraordinary items, and profit or loss before tax, reconciled to statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts must reflect the Spanish company's own accounts. Foreign parent-company accounts must not be consolidated into the SL return unless a specific tax-consolidation or reporting rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary accounting-to-tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, impairment, related-party adjustments, exempt income, and capitalization or reserve deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish domestic-law adjustments to the SL's Spanish taxable base. Foreign tax adjustments are relevant only when they affect income or expenses recorded by the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose or adjust transactions with related parties where the arm's-length value differs from the booked amount, including goods, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and restructuring charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border dealings with a non-resident parent, affiliate, or common-control company must be supported by contemporaneous Spanish transfer-pricing documentation and substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter available tax losses, losses utilized in the current period, and remaining balances, subject to statutory percentage limitations and the minimum tax rules applicable to larger companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses belong to the Spanish SL and cannot normally be transferred to a foreign shareholder or affiliate outside an applicable Spanish tax-consolidation regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying deductions and credits, including R&D and technological innovation, double-taxation relief, job-creation incentives, donations, and other statutory items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent incentives cannot be claimed by the SL unless the Spanish legislation specifically grants the relief and the SL satisfies the evidentiary requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income, tax rate, gross liability, and net liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable base, applicable rate, gross corporate tax, deductions, withholding credits, instalment payments, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish resident-company rate. Withholding suffered by the SL may be creditable only where Spanish law permits and the income is included in the tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile Modelo 202 instalments, Spanish withholding tax, advance payments, and other creditable amounts against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax is generally claimed under Spanish double-taxation relief rules, subject to statutory limits, proof of payment, and income inclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare amount payable, refund, zero balance, direct-debit instructions, or payment reference generated by AEAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment from a non-Spanish bank is possible through AEAT-approved procedures, but the taxpayer remains responsible for the Spanish filing reference and settlement deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Accounts, shareholder, related-party, and tax-incentive annexes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable supplementary schedules and electronically provide required accounting and tax information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign shareholders, group relationships, related-party balances, and cross-border transactions accurately; do not omit beneficial-owner or group information merely because the owner is non-resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay where the taxpayer files voluntarily within 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus statutory late-payment interest from the end of that 12-month period. Failure to file or materially incorrect filing may trigger fixed or proportional penalties under the General Tax Law, commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid tax or improperly obtained refund. Penalties may be reduced for conformity, prompt payment, or voluntary correction where statutory conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account; filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalment filings in April, October, and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The normal filing windows are 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. The exact period is adjusted when the final day is a non-business day. Large companies and taxpayers using the alternative tax-base method calculate instalments under the applicable statutory method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, instalment period, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and corporate-tax period. A foreign shareholder is not the filer unless it separately has a Spanish permanent establishment or other Spanish filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the prior-year tax-liability method or, where mandatory or elected, the current-period tax-base method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border income, deductions, and related-party adjustments must be reflected in the Spanish SL's current-period base where the alternative method applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Prior-period liability or current-period taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the statutory reference amount used to calculate the instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use the foreign parent company's tax liability or consolidated group base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter creditable withholding amounts, prior instalments, applicable percentage, and amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Spanish-law creditable amounts attributable to the SL may reduce the instalment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the payment reference, direct debit, or zero-result filing where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of payment and the AEAT submission receipt for audit purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late voluntary filing with payment generally produces the same 1% plus 1% per complete month surcharge structure, with a 15% surcharge after 12 months plus interest. Failure to pay an assessed instalment may lead to enforcement surcharges, interest, attachment of assets, and penalties for tax infringement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, informative declaration of related-party transactions and transactions with tax havens or non-cooperative jurisdictions; filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, where statutory thresholds or reporting categories are met
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal period is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, and applicable reporting sections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish SL and disclose foreign related parties using the information required for the relevant transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify transactions as financing, services, goods, property, royalties, leases, guarantees, or other controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border purchases and sales of polyethylene or polypropylene, intercompany financing, guarantees, management services, and intellectual-property charges must be classified consistently with the agreements and accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the related party, country, relationship, transaction type, amount, and valuation basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the legal counterparty and ultimate relevant jurisdiction; do not substitute an intermediary where beneficial ownership or control is different.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply statutory transaction-type and counterparty thresholds, including the general EUR 250,000 aggregate threshold with the same related person or entity and specific thresholds for certain transaction categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate transactions by related counterparty and category as required. Transactions involving non-cooperative jurisdictions require heightened review and may trigger additional disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions falling within the statutory reporting category involving jurisdictions designated under Spanish law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm current Spanish designation lists and beneficial ownership before making payments or recording expenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or inaccurate informative reporting may produce statutory fixed or per-data penalties and may increase audit risk. Incorrect reporting can also support a transfer-pricing adjustment, denial of deduction, withholding assessment, or anti-abuse challenge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring at least a 5% participation or qualifying acquisition value, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, subject-to-tax and legal-form conditions, and anti-abuse requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse conditions where relevant, ownership and holding-period evidence, and absence of conduit arrangements. Apply the reduced treaty rate or exemption at source only where the payer has sufficient documentation and Spanish procedural requirements are satisfied. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. Maintain board resolutions, dividend vouchers, ownership records, residence certificates, and evidence of economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident withholding rate is generally 24% for Spanish-source income paid to non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment, with a 19% rate generally applying to certain EU or EEA residents that satisfy the statutory conditions. Interest and royalties paid to an associated EU company may qualify for exemption under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring a qualifying legal form, minimum 25% direct participation or qualifying common ownership, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, subject-to-tax status, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse compliance. Applicable tax treaties may reduce or eliminate withholding, commonly providing lower rates for interest and royalties, but the exact rate depends on the recipient's residence country and treaty. Arm's-length pricing, beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, and Spanish-source characterization must be documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish transfer-pricing documentation is generally required for controlled transactions, subject to statutory exemptions. A principal exemption applies where the aggregate controlled transactions with the same related person or entity do not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length during the tax period, excluding specified transactions and subject to the documentation regulations. A local file is generally required for material controlled transactions; a master file is generally required for Spanish entities forming part of a group subject to the applicable country-by-country reporting framework, with simplified documentation rules for smaller groups. Modelo 232 has separate reporting thresholds, including the general EUR 250,000 counterparty threshold and specific thresholds for certain categories.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a standalone jurisdiction-wide Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the UAE or certain offshore jurisdictions. Economic substance remains material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the principal-purpose and anti-abuse rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, the anti-hybrid rules, controlled foreign company rules, EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest-Royalties Directive anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership analysis, and permanent-establishment principles. A Spanish SL distributing petrochemical products should maintain real management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under effective control, premises or verifiable logistics capability, inventory and risk management, bank and accounting controls, commercially supportable contracts, and decision-making evidence. Empty conduit structures, circular financing, non-arm's-length margins, artificial royalty or interest charges, and unsupported management fees are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, falsifying invoices, deducting fictitious purchases, understating inventory or margins, using sham service or royalty agreements, or deliberately omitting taxable income so that the tax liability is defrauded by more than EUR 120,000 in a tax year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud generally carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, together with restitution and loss of public subsidies or tax benefits. Aggravated cases, including fraud exceeding EUR 600,000, organized conduct, or use of interposed persons, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded. Administrative assessments, interest, and penalties may apply separately where criminal prosecution is not pursued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they knowingly participate, authorize, facilitate, or fail to prevent the offense. They may face imprisonment, fines, civil restitution, disqualification from public office or benefits, and personal tax liability under Spanish General Tax Law derivative-liability provisions. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court where legally justified; there is no automatic travel ban solely because a tax return is late.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for cross-border polymer purchases or sales, excessive related-party financing, unsupported guarantees, inflated management fees, artificial royalties, or deliberate allocation of profit to a low-tax affiliate without operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, corresponding adjustment, secondary adjustment, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, charge late-payment interest, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide documentation or providing materially false or incomplete documentation may attract penalties calculated by reference to data or adjusted amounts, subject to statutory caps and minimums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may become jointly or subsidiarily liable for assessed tax, penalties, or collection costs where statutory negligence, collaboration, asset stripping, or enforcement-obstruction conditions are met. Criminal exposure may arise if the conduct also satisfies the tax-fraud threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoices, VAT fraud, and carousel fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for non-existent goods, manipulating intra-community acquisitions, claiming input VAT without economic activity, misdescribing polymer quantities or origin, or participating in chains designed to disappear with VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, denial of input credit, proportional penalties linked to the improperly deducted or unpaid VAT, interest, seizure, and possible criminal prosecution apply. Tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold may result in imprisonment and fines; customs and excise sanctions may also apply where import declarations are false.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face criminal liability, personal civil restitution, derivative tax liability, disqualification, and asset-seizure measures. Travel restrictions can be ordered in criminal proceedings where necessary to secure the process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding-tax failure and unlawful profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, commissions, or service fees to non-residents without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate or beneficial ownership, or using conduit entities to obtain an exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unwithheld amount, late-payment interest, and withholding-related penalties. Treaty or EU relief may be denied, and anti-abuse rules may recharacterize the payment or recipient. Repeated or fraudulent non-withholding can create broader tax-fraud exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur derivative liability where they caused or negligently permitted the failure, particularly during liquidation or asset distributions. Knowing participation in fraudulent repatriation may create criminal and civil liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial-owner concealment, or artificial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real personnel, decision-making, inventory, logistics, or commercial risk; concealing the ultimate beneficial owner; routing payments through nominee entities; or using a Spanish SL solely to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authorities may deny treaty or EU exemptions, apply the general anti-abuse rule, recharacterize transactions, deny deductions, assess tax and interest, impose tax penalties, and refer conduct for criminal investigation where fraud thresholds are met. Corporate-law and insolvency consequences may also arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto controllers may be liable for tax debts, damages to creditors, unlawful distributions, concealment, and criminal offenses. Courts may disregard separate legal personality in exceptional cases involving abuse, fraud, or creditor prejudice; imprisonment and judicial travel restrictions are possible only where criminal-law conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify customers and beneficial owners, accepting opaque payment structures, processing suspicious third-party payments, ignoring sanctioned-country or sanctioned-counterparty indicators, or misdeclaring the origin, destination, end use, or classification of petrochemical products.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish anti-money-laundering law, serious and very serious infringements may produce public or private warnings, substantial monetary fines, management disqualification, publication measures, and possible suspension or withdrawal of authorization where applicable. Criminal money laundering may carry imprisonment generally from 6 months to 6 years, fines, confiscation, and enhanced sanctions for aggravated conduct. EU and Spanish sanctions breaches may generate administrative and criminal consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and responsible managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted for knowing participation, authorization, or serious supervisory failure. Confiscation, civil restitution, disqualification, asset freezing, and court-ordered travel restrictions may apply in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying polyethylene or polypropylene granules, understating customs value, falsifying origin, using incorrect Incoterms, evading import VAT, or using preferential origin documentation without satisfying origin rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, interest, seizure, administrative fines, loss of simplified customs procedures, and potential criminal customs fraud sanctions may apply. The company may also lose commercial or customs-authorized-operator privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may incur civil and administrative liability and, for deliberate fraud, criminal liability, confiscation, disqualification, and restitution obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep reliable accounting records, failure to legalize books or file annual accounts, concealment of related-party balances, destruction of supporting records, or using accounts inconsistent with customs, VAT, banking, and corporate-tax data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties, denial of deductions, presumptive assessments, audit extensions, accounting sanctions, potential commercial-registry consequences, and insolvency or creditor claims may arise. Destruction or falsification of records can become a criminal offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability to the company and creditors, derivative tax liability, insolvency disqualification, restitution, and criminal liability for deliberate falsification or concealment.
